chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, the servant may be righteous to his parents during their lifetime, then they die, but he does not pay off their debts on their behalf, nor seeks forgiveness for them, so Allah writes him as unrighteous; and indeed, he may be unrighteous to them during their lifetime, not being righteous with them, but when they die, he pays off their debt and seeks forgiveness for them, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes him as righteous.
ai.seo_question: How does paying parents' debts and seeking forgiveness after their death affect one's spiritual status in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the dynamic nature of filial piety (birr al-walidayn) by contrasting the spiritual status of a child who is righteous in life but neglectful in death versus one who is neglectful in life but dutiful in death. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on posthumous obligations, such as settling debts and seeking forgiveness (istighfar), as decisive factors in determining the final spiritual record of the offspring.
